name: Sellfy
summary: No-code store builder for creators to sell digital products, subscriptions and print-on-demand merch, with zero transaction fees and built-in social-media selling.
best_for: creators selling digital products, subscriptions and print-on-demand who want a simple store with zero platform commission
skip_if: you sell occasionally (percentage-fee platforms like Gumroad cost nothing idle), or you need a full e-commerce platform (Shopify territory)
honest_knock: The honest mechanic is the revenue ladder: plans cap by your ANNUAL SALES, so success moves you up. But the caps are soft - Sellfy's FAQ says it may charge 2% on revenue above your limit rather than forcing an upgrade, so ask whether that applies to you before jumping a tier. The 0% transaction fee is rare and beats percentage-taking platforms at volume; below a few hundred in monthly sales the flat subscription is the tax instead, and your processor still takes about 2.9% + 30c regardless.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter, up to $10k in sales · billed monthly
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-07, 2026-09-30 and 2026-11-21) Starter is $29/mo billed monthly or $22/mo billed yearly, for up to $10k of sales a year; Business $79 or $59, up to $50k; Premium $159 or $119, up to $200k; above that Sellfy quotes you. Yearly billing saves 25%, there is a 14-day trial, a 30-day money-back guarantee and no free tier. 0% transaction fees on every plan, though PayPal or Stripe still take roughly 2.9% + 30c per transaction. The revenue limits are soft: Sellfy's own pricing.md says the store is never suspended and you are never forced to upgrade, while the page's FAQ says you are expected to upgrade and that Sellfy may instead charge a 2% overage fee on revenue above the limit. Read in US dollars from a Netherlands connection. Re-read on 21 November 2026 on sellfy.com/pricing/ and sellfy.com/pricing.md: Starter $29/$22, Business $79/$59 and Premium $159/$119 with the $10k, $50k and $200k sales limits are unchanged. The pricing.md file (still dated 5 August 2026) now states both halves in one place: the limits are soft caps measured per billing year, the store stays live, and Sellfy may charge a 2% overage fee on revenue above the limit if you have not upgraded. It also lists the per-plan file-size caps (10, 15 and 20 GB) and free email credits (2,000, 10,000 and 50,000 a month). Re-read 24 November 2026 on sellfy.com/pricing/ and sellfy.com/pricing.md (still dated 5 August 2026): Starter $29/$22, Business $79/$59 and Premium $159/$119 with the $10k, $50k and $200k sales limits, the 2% overage fee, the 10/15/20 GB file caps and the 2,000/10,000/50,000 email credits are all unchanged.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session made and published a digital product of $5 with a test file in Sellfy under the free 14 day trial, without a card and without any payment connection, in about 2 minutes and 9 steps. During the trial the public store shows Launching soon and is not available to shop at, and the buyer checkout says that customers can't yet purchase until you upgrade; to test checkout you must also connect Stripe or PayPal. The prices are unchanged against the dossier (Starter $29 monthly or $22 yearly, Business $79 or $59, Premium $159 or $119, all plus 21% VAT) and the Starter checkout showed Tax (21%) $6.09 and Total due now: $35.09. Inside the app the limit is only shown as Up to $10k in sales per year; the 2% overage from the dossier is on the public FAQ but not in the app. Nothing was paid and the account was not deleted. Account and start: the account was created by us and was signed in in his Chrome (the interface was already in English); our AI assistant ran the test from 15:07 (Amsterdam). The dossier name is Sellfy and the review is on MSS (mss/sellfy-review.html). The audiences from the dossier: Creators selling digital products steadily, and Creators whose sales pass the plan limit. Onboarding at the start: What do you want to sell? was answered with Digital downloads/streams, the product category with Fitness & Sports, and in Customize your store the made up name Sample Snowboards Shop was entered in place of the default name, then the button Done!. The dashboard showed Getting started, 1 out of 6 steps completed and Trial ends in 14 days. Core action: Add new product offers Digital product, Print On Demand, Subscription, Physical product, Bundle and Freebie. A Digital product was made with the title Test Wax Guide (PDF), the price 5.00 USD and a test file of 2.1KB under the tab Content. Hurdle: the first upload went to the picture field by mistake, because of the wrong file input; the page was reloaded and the file was added again through the file field. Publish product worked without a payment connection, with the message Congrats on your first product! (You've successfully uploaded your first product!). From the start at 15:07 the product was published at about 15:09, so about 2 minutes and 9 steps. Public store: for a visitor the store shows Launching soon... This store is on a free trial and isn't available to shop at, yet. So during the trial the store is not public. The owner preview through View my store works: a banner This is your store, the product at $5, a Buy now button and 1 file (2.1KB). Checkout as a buyer (/checkout/details/): the notice The store checkout is available to test, but customers can't yet purchase. For customers to purchase, please upgrade. Fields: Email and the optional tick for product updates; Order summary Test Wax Guide (PDF) $5, Subtotal $5, Total US$5 and the button Continue. Nothing was filled in. Payment settings (not connected): Add payment methods to test checkout. To enable checkout for your customers, please upgrade. The options are Stripe (Create a free Stripe account or Connect an existing Stripe account, Recommended) and PayPal (Connect with PayPal). So a connection is needed to test a purchase with a real payment method, and a paid plan is needed to let customers buy; making a product and viewing the store works without them. Plans: Select your plan under Billing, read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 under the trial, in US dollars with +21% VAT added. Starter $29/mo billed monthly or $22/mo billed yearly ($348 struck through, $264 billed yearly); Business $79/mo or $59/mo ($948 struck through, $708 billed yearly); Premium $159/mo or $119/mo ($1,908 struck through, $1,428 billed yearly). Limits: Up to $10k, Up to $50k and Up to $200k in sales per year, with a line for more than $200k to contact the vendor. The comparison table says Transaction fees 0% on all three plans, a maximum file size of 10GB, 15GB and 20GB and 2,000, 10,000 and 50,000 email credits; the money back guarantee is a full refund within 30 days from your upgrade. Select plan Starter on monthly billing opened Sellfy Checkout: Starter $29.00 / mo, Tax (21%) $6.09, Total due now: $35.09, with credit card or PayPal, and the line Upgrading will end your free trial. The tester filled in nothing and paid nothing. The public page sellfy.com/pricing was read again just before this delivery the same day, with the Monthly and Yearly switch: yearly $22, $59 and $119 a month (save 25%), limits of $10,000, $50,000 and $200,000 in sales a year, transaction fees 0%, and the FAQ line that monthly billing costs $29 for Starter, $79 for Business and $159 for Premium. The prices are therefore UNCHANGED against the dossier (Starter $29 monthly or $22 yearly). Deviations against the dossier: the public FAQ and the dossier say that Sellfy may charge 2% on the sales above the limit of your plan, but the plan and billing pages inside the app only say Up to $10k in sales per year and show no 2% overage, soft cap or forced upgrade. The trial is 14 days without a card and ends automatically on 02-12-2026. Billing page: Trial 14 days left. Your trial will end automatically on 02-12-2026. Payment method: Credit card not provided. Billing history shows one line, #1265659, November 18, 2026, $0.00, Paid. No card was needed for the trial. Cancelling: there is no subscription to cancel, the trial ends by itself. The account settings page has a section Delete account: Your account and order information and any uploaded files will be permanently removed from Sellfy. These can't be recovered. The button Delete account was not clicked. Not tested: a real purchase, Stripe and PayPal, the 0% fee in practice, the overage above $10k, email marketing, a domain, changing the theme, bundles and subscription products. Clean up: the account and the test store Sample Snowboards Shop with the product Test Wax Guide (PDF) remain (trial, not live); no payment provider was connected and nothing was bought; the browser tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: During the trial your store is not public and customers can't buy, so you cannot do a real first sale before you pay for a plan; the owner preview and the test checkout do work. Testing the checkout needs a Stripe or PayPal connection. The first file upload can land in the picture field, because there are two file inputs. Inside the app only Up to $10k in sales per year is shown, while the public FAQ and the dossier mention a possible 2% overage above the limit. All prices are plus 21% VAT: Starter monthly came to $35.09 due now.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: A real purchase, and the connection of Stripe or PayPal.
The 0% transaction fee in practice, and what happens above $10k in sales (the 2% overage was not reached).
Email marketing, a custom domain, theme changes, bundles and subscription products.
Cancelling a paid plan, because nothing was bought; the account was not deleted.
Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.

Session and source-reading date: 18 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 15:07 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.
exit_test.note: A check of this export route with synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Re-importing the export was not tested. The exported file was not opened, so what it contains is unverified. Friction is described, not scored; this is not a verdict on the product.
